units.title: Numbers, HCF and LCM, Ratio, Percentage and Average
topics: Integers, primes, divisibility, remainders, even and odd results
HCF and LCM and their word problems

sections.title: Integers, primes, divisibility, remainders, even and odd results
HCF and LCM and their word problems

summary: Check divisibility by digit sums and last digits before dividing; primes up to 120 need testing by 2, 3, 5, 7 only.
n(n+1) is always even; n^3-n is always a multiple of 6.
HCF × LCM equals the product of the two numbers, and of no other count of numbers.
"Greatest divisor" means HCF of the differences from the remainders; "least number" means LCM plus the remainder.
Chain ratios by matching the common term, then divide in parts.
Percentage change is always on the base the question names; successive changes multiply.
A 25 % rise is undone by a 20 % fall, not a 25 % fall.
For averages, deal in totals, not in averages.

Time and work, pipes and cisterns
Speed, distance, time, trains and boats
Area, perimeter and volume of plane and solid figures
Eight traps in profit, interest, work, speed and mixture questions

summary: Profit and loss use the cost price; discount uses the marked price.
Mark up 25 % and discount 20 % gives no gain, no loss.
For two years, compound interest exceeds simple interest by P(R/100)^2.
Two workers together take ab/(a+b) days; a leaking pipe subtracts its rate.
36 km/h is 10 m/s; multiply by 5/18 to go from km/h to m/s.
Average speed over equal distances is the harmonic mean, never the simple mean.
A train crossing a platform covers its own length plus the platform.
Alligation gives the ratio directly as the two differences across the cross.

Functions, domain, range, composite and inverse functions

sections.title: Sets, subsets, operations and Venn-diagram word problems
Functions, domain, range, composite and inverse functions
Eight traps in sets, relations and functions

summary: Count with n(A∪ B)=n(A)+n(B)-n(A∩ B); "neither" is the total minus the union.
A set of n elements has 2^n subsets, one of them the empty set.
A-B means A∩ B'.
Equivalence = reflexive + symmetric + transitive.
A function gives each input exactly one output; check one-one and onto separately.
Domain: no zero denominators, no negative square roots, positive log arguments.
To invert, swap x and y; to compose, work from the inside out.

units.title: Indices, Logarithms, Polynomials and Quadratic Equations
topics: Quadratic equations, nature and sum and product of roots
Linear and simultaneous equations, inequalities, equation word problems

sections.title: Quadratic equations, nature and sum and product of roots
Linear and simultaneous equations, inequalities, equation word problems
Eight traps in indices, logarithms, polynomials and equations

summary: Reduce to a common base before equating indices.
log(m+n) cannot be split; log(mn) can.
D decides the nature of roots; D=0 gives equal roots.
Use α+β and αβ instead of solving for the roots.
f(a) is the remainder on division by (x-a).
A negative multiplier reverses an inequality.
Always substitute back after squaring.

units.title: Sequences and Series

sections.title: Eight traps in sequences and series

summary: Count terms first: n=(l-a)/(d)+1.
Sn for AP is n times the average of first and last.
Use (a)/(r),a,ar for three GP numbers and a-d,a,a+d for AP.
S_∞ exists only when |r|<1.
an=Sn-Sn-1 recovers terms from sums.
AM≥ GM, with equality only when the numbers are equal.

units.title: Matrices and Determinants
topics: Types, order and operations on matrices
Adjoint, inverse and solution of linear systems

sections.title: Types, order and operations on matrices
Eight traps in matrices and determinants

summary: Order m× n: m rows, n columns; a column holds m elements.
AB exists only if inner orders match, and AB≠ BA in general.
A zero determinant means singular: no inverse, and a row dependency.
|kA|=k^n|A|: the factor is raised to the order.
Reverse the order for (AB)^T and (AB)^-1.
Use Cramer's rule when D≠0.

topics: Fundamental principle of counting, permutations and combinations
Mean, median, mode and measures of dispersion

sections.title: Eight traps in counting, probability and statistics

summary: Order matters: permutation. Order does not matter: combination.
Divide by factorials of repeated letters.
Subtract from the total for "at least one".
Independent events multiply; overlapping events subtract the intersection.
SD ignores a constant shift.

units.title: Trigonometry
topics: Trigonometric ratios, standard angles and identities

sections.title: Trigonometric ratios, standard angles and identities

summary: Memorise the 0°–90° table; every other value reduces to it.
Complementary angles swap sin with cos, tan with cot.
Three forms of cos2A; pick the one that fits the data.
General solution needs nπ for tan and sine, 2nπ for cosine.
In height problems, draw a right triangle and use tan.

Angle between lines, parallel and perpendicular lines, distance of a point from a line

sections.title: Slope and forms of the equation of a line
Angle between lines, parallel and perpendicular lines, distance from a point
Eight traps in the straight line

summary: Use d=√Δ x^2+Δ y^2; memorise 3-4-5 and 5-12-13.
Convert Ax+By+C=0 to slope -A/B.
Intercept form needs both intercepts non-zero.
Parallel lines have equal slopes; perpendicular slopes multiply to -1.
In the point-line formula the denominator is √A^2+B^2.

Parabola, ellipse and hyperbola in standard form

sections.title: Parabola, ellipse and hyperbola in standard form
Eight traps in circles and conics

summary: Complete the square or use g,f,c to read a circle off its equation.
For y^2=4ax read a from the coefficient: y^2=12x gives a=3.
Ellipse: e<1; hyperbola: e>1.
Major axis follows the larger denominator.
Tangent length is √S1, the power of the point.

sections.title: Vector algebra, position vectors and unit vectors
Dot product, cross product and their applications

summary: A vector from A to B is B-A.
Dot product gives a number, cross product gives a vector.
Perpendicular means dot product zero.
|atimesb| is a parallelogram area.
Unit vectors are found by dividing by the magnitude.

units.title: Limits and Differentiation
topics: Limits of algebraic and trigonometric functions

sections.title: Limits of algebraic and trigonometric functions
Eight traps in limits and differentiation

summary: Substitute, then factor or use a standard limit for (0)/(0).
lim(|sin x|)/(x) does not exist at 0.
Differentiate by the product rule when two functions of x multiply.
Stationary points need f'=0; the sign of f'' decides the type.
Rates multiply by the chain rule.

units.title: Integration

sections.title: Methods: substitution and integration by parts

summary: Add +C to every indefinite integral and omit it in definite ones.
∫(1)/(x)dx=ln|x|, not x^0.
An odd function over a symmetric interval integrates to zero.
Use parts when a product has a log, inverse-trig or x× e^x.
Area under y=x^2 from 0 to 3 is 9.

units.title: Verbal and Logical Reasoning
summary: Decode with the first letter, test on the second.
Draw the family tree; take one link at a time.
Right turn clockwise, left turn anticlockwise.
Rankings overlap by exactly one person.
A conclusion must follow from the statements alone.

topics: Number and letter series, odd one out

sections.title: Number and letter series, odd one out
Eight traps in reasoning series and counting

summary: Check first and second differences, then squares, cubes, primes.
Count odd days, then take the remainder by 7.
Century years are leap only if divisible by 400.
Use 5.5M for the clock; reduce reflex angles.
Count squares of every size, not just the smallest.
